title: Thoughts on Astra?
author: AshlaStudios
selftext:
I think it might be a good idea to have a thread where everyone could share their experience with the newest model released in comparison to the most recent prominent ones. In context of various aspects of development. So for example how does Astra compare to Fable/Opus in terms of:  
\- Asset Generation   
\- UI/UX Design  
\- Game Balance  
\- Programming  
etc. 

What are your thoughts on Astra so far? Is it actually outperforming Claude in everything?

comments.author: EchoingAngel
comments.body: I'm mostly using it to correct weirdness from Sol, but as far as handling new issues on its own, it's okay. Astra high is taking about as long as Sol would and still breaks things. The main win I've had from it so far is cleaning up phrasing and naming schemes Sol made up that were terrible AI slop and were going to need me to rewrite eventually.

comments.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
comments.body: Apparently it's browser use is unmatched meaning you can have it actually use a drawing program and make art forreal. I'll  be getting around to see if it can make real pixel art. Not generations.

replies.author: DaleRobinson
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/6rzdxdyq0qnh1.png?width=960&format=png&auto=webp&s=7e5f4c95a021237ec580f6102a0b20f593d94024

it drew this in Aseprite, with 18 layers inside of 5 separate folders.

replies.author: DaleRobinson
replies.body: It's fascinating. On one hand there are some parts I think look incredible and it even used proper shading techniques/dithering. Then there are the janky looking trees and some weird details that become more noticeable the more you look. I told it to draw this inside of a 320x224 canvas.

replies.author: Anxious_Marsupial_59
replies.body: did it use a MCP or was it directly?

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
With my plan it's basically unusable. With sol high i can work a normal developer  pace with healthy breaks. With sol I can have it do a task, take my mind off, 1 to 10 mins later creak if the feature or change works. Then repeat and do that for about 3 to 4 hours. Which is a normal deep coding work day for an established project.

Sol doesn't screw up that much unless I ask it to do to much at once, or I'm asking to big a task close to limit.

With Astra low I ask it 2 things and it's burned the whole 5 hour budget. I'd hate to see how much it cost paying for credits. Then there are Astras quirks. Its not great at web design yet and my game uses a js html engine, so it will stick extra text and buttons where they don't belong and do things I didn't ask for or break the css like it's a junior.

I just don't like it generally, it feels like running sol on extra high which doesn't give any more performance. Both are just cost prohibitive to use and overkill for the level of work and directions I'm giving.

comments.author: eschaff2114
comments.body: I’d say to make sure you set limits on it while it runs. I’m trying to build a knitting engine and it ran for 5 hours doing scientific calculations to make the engine and used like 30% of my weekly usage, mostly cause it was just running so many computations. But it’s been able to move further on the engine than Sol was. Sol was lost for this for me, even with a scientific paper and a git repository. My hope is to use it in my game 😊

comments.author: M1ghtyMe
comments.body: Underwhelming for me. Was expecting stronger 3d asset creation but still only 40% there were i wanted to be vs reference image, after running already for 5+ hr loop

comments.author: SnuffleBag
comments.body: Yes, IMO it’s outperforming Claude in everything except creativity, design and writing. Despite the scary 2.5x cost it’s both substantially faster, and substantially cheaper than Fable for me.
